title: Demand in Carbon Credit Market Continues, Says Artemeter CEO
content: Olivia Albrecht, Founder and CEO of Artemeter, says that despite the Trump administration's energy policies, corporates and other clients continue buying carbon credits, but are focusing on long-term strategies. Albrecht also discusses the renewable energy space, government subsidies, and more, on Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. She speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: FAT Brands and Creditors Tap Advisers for Restructuring Talks
content: Restaurant chain owner FAT Brands Inc. and its creditors are working with advisers to discuss a potential restructuring of its roughly $1.2 billion of whole business securitization debt, according to people with knowledge of the discussions.

title: Powell Says No 'Risk-Free' Path, Trump's UN Rebuff | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 9/23/2025
content: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss Fed Chair Jerome Powell's remarks reiterating there is no 'risk-free' policy path ahead for the central bank. Bloomberg's Michael McKee joins to break it down. Also on today's show, Bloomberg News Senior White House Correspondent Josh Wingrove talks President Trump's combative United Nations speech, CSIS Middle East Program Director & Senior Adviser Mona Yacoubian on Canada and the United Kingdom breaking with Trump and recognizing a Palestinian state, and Artemeter Chief Executive Officer Olivia Albrecht examines carbon credits as an asset class. (Source: Bloomberg)
